name: the play administered: steps that test, police, end and convert the April Fools frame
what_it_changes: K01 states that the host sub is keyed as play for April Fools and that a claim in it may be a joke. In these rooms the frame gains steps that the statement does not hold. Members test whether a claim is a joke by its date, source or link. They police the licence's limits and argue about when it ends. Moderators enforce a takeover's rules by real removals and switch its styling off. A joke can turn into a sincere request or a lasting change. The steps belong to the sub's own play beside the canvas, not to canvas work.
why: Cut rules R1 and R2 (tree-D4.md). add-step lines on K01 meet at T4-001 (Keying) in 103 rooms: 164 lines, 104 ruled elaboration and 60 specification (the kind is not relied on). They meet at nine level-3 nodes, so the group holds at the fourth order, and it is declared there. Read whole in _analysis/d4a01_lines_K01_addstep.txt (d4_key_lines.py): every line adds a step of handling the frame. Testing: 'Recipients test dates, links and hidden text' (fivenightsatfreddys). Policing: 'Participants police the scope of licensed joking' (bostonceltics). Ending: 'Moderators settle the prank's cutoff by timezone' (warframe). Enforcing: 'Fictional commandments are enforced through real removals and approvals' (battlecats). Converting: 'Participants explicitly convert an apparent joke poll into a real continuing activity' (kanye). These are the labelers' how sentences, not members' words. Many lines say that the step is not canvas work ('rather than continuation of a canvas collective', 4chan).
